Approved findings

Approved evidence · As of 12 Nov 2026

aa-lcr · human annotation: AA-LCR’s creator describes undergraduate question writers using non-frontier models to screen difficulty, followed by human testing on the same document sets, revision or removal of failed questions, and at least one correct human solution for every retained question.

candidate.third11.aa-lcr.curation.v2

  • This is the creator’s reported construction and validation procedure, not an assertion that each question has unanimous human agreement.

Approved evidence · As of 12 Nov 2026

aa-lcr · evaluates: The pinned AA-LCR card uses an LLM equality checker with instructions for numerical equivalence, required formats, ordering and a single committed final answer; it identifies GPT-5.6 Luna at medium reasoning as the checker.

candidate.third11.aa-lcr.scoring.v2

  • Mercor’s separately captured AA-LCRv 1.1 implementation specifies Gemini 3.5 Flash, four repeats and pass@1 aggregated across repeats rather than a best-of score. The two judge configurations are preserved separately.

Approved evidence · As of 12 Nov 2026

aa-lcr · dataset size: The pinned AA-LCR creator card describes 100 text questions over 30 document sets containing 234 documents, with about 100,000 input tokens per document set.

candidate.third11.aa-lcr.units.v2

  • Questions require reasoning across documents rather than direct retrieval; questions, document sets and documents are different units of one family.

Approved evidence · As of 12 Nov 2026

aa-lcr · documents: AA-LCR version 1.1 corrects sixteen answer keys and adds an equality-checker system prompt while leaving the questions and document sets unchanged; the creator says version 1.0.0 and 1.1 scores are not directly comparable.

candidate.third11.aa-lcr.version.v2

  • Four answer-key repairs change the answer itself; the remaining repairs address notation or units. These revisions are manifestations of the retained family.
